### 2026-11-03: Project research (the process what I learnt how and why):

**4h**

Project research (the process what I learnt how and why):

Before I even signed up to do this particular project I was already asking myself, how does a distortion pedal work and also how can we use circuitry to make this distortion.

And so I went into research on how this process actually worked.

Firstly I went on youtube to see what videos might explain to me the process of distortion and so I started off with this video:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/O3Acm6SNVObwxoygu6eLOTWIyDAUs5vl/cfc3805589648c5ded148aeecf5d2a43f78a43baaf75e578056fe97d8c125a5e.png)

Even though I already knew that distortion was the clipping of audio, this was helpful in reminding me about how the waveform is meant to change in the process of distortion.

I learnt that distortion is normally developed by clipping the tops of sound waves where the peaks are, turning the signal more and more into a square wave:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/O3Acm6SNVObwxoygu6eLOTWIyDAUs5vl/4acd4985801c9dbf75ea0a724bcc77857589019c984a5b1815cf239a410207ff.png)

I already know clarinet is a pure square wave due to the way it is structured and am curious to why distortion doesn't seem to make a guitar sound like a clarinet but I will learn about that eventually.

I then went to find myself a guide on how to build a distortion circuit and went through an array of videos and guides to try build one. In the end I settled for this:

https://curiousmotor.com/2019/12/07/distortion-pedal-electronics-explained/

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/O3Acm6SNVObwxoygu6eLOTWIyDAUs5vl/e2c093dddbd7037c375dd9858b93af7ecb9506c7200648bb296f0603dc67c533.png)

I chose this mainly because it seemed to describe a lot about the reasons why distortion worked, had a lot of helpful video guides and had schematics that seemed to look like proper schematics.

Though I had now found myself a guide that seemed to work, I was still very curious about the process of distortion generally and went to understand the specifics behind how it worked in circuitry.

Firstly I went to discover the use of diode clipping through a video like this (I can't find the original):

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=16Vz6XHqGMY

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/O3Acm6SNVObwxoygu6eLOTWIyDAUs5vl/a0e9098df070da3dfc65f01e66f8853cf997c43f8804236323beedb70dd3a5d6.png)

And also went to understand more about how diodes were used in circuits using this video:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/O3Acm6SNVObwxoygu6eLOTWIyDAUs5vl/fd95bc3d151e2a7a6fd299d329c31d873ef856bde17f966e977e4753b343fdf9.png)

This helped me to understand why distortion happened but I still wanted a bit of practice in understanding the equations behind diode clipping. To do this I went and used this organicchemistrytutor video which gave me questions and helped me to practice my understanding of diodes:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/O3Acm6SNVObwxoygu6eLOTWIyDAUs5vl/7a8371cb178755bd41b745b235a9de0ecb3870b8ffec024fd61d50d4c0aa0397.png)

This greatly helped me to understand exactly why clipping occurs because of the diode and can change the waveform once the amplitude reaches more than 0.7V.

I was still confused on how transistors work and what they do and what they are as well, lol:

So I went and found myself resources to teach me about how transistors work inside of the circuit such as:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/O3Acm6SNVObwxoygu6eLOTWIyDAUs5vl/242044d57675b268640db387a6d65395cbb6bac00825afdfbe9a91f1005b0afa.png)

and:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/O3Acm6SNVObwxoygu6eLOTWIyDAUs5vl/33d6fec5e3d62a383dc063be083811a5b4f512c04b18c2e2b8cf5645e7275cc4.png)

Through all this I learnt how transistors can be used to switch components on and off in computing circuitry, but also it can be used to amplify signals which I will be doing in a distortion circuit.

I could distort sound by going through the transistor and overloading it, however I know this will cause a heat problem that I do not want to deal with and also it may damage components and spend money on heat paste.

Even though I knew what a cpacitor was, I was still unsure on how to apply this to a circuit, so I went and learnt their application more properly by looking at this organic chemistry tutor video:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/O3Acm6SNVObwxoygu6eLOTWIyDAUs5vl/4f88eb5d2149a6f0045043baf20f4b7842e71e002481dd26d92db123b3debea6.png)

and:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/O3Acm6SNVObwxoygu6eLOTWIyDAUs5vl/32602cc5377f989943836b0b093a44b6e6943fb80e6ba51682131c0c22819523.png)

I also learnt in this video specifically, how to use transistors as inverters even though I was not going to use that.

There were many more relavant videos but I wasn't going to list and watch all of them.

Now I had a general understanding of how distortion worked, how amplification from transistors worked, how the maths worked and how to put the whole system together.

Time to build this in reality:

### 2026-11-07: Today I am going to see where I can find the parts: but before that I was advised on Slack that instead of using the switch I was currently using (which would simply turn the system off and on) I shou

**1h**

Today I am going to see where I can find the parts: but before that I was advised on Slack that instead of using the switch I was currently using (which would simply turn the system off and on) I should learn about DPDT true bypass wiring and use that instead, so I am going to try to do that.

Research DPDT True pybass wiring:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/O3Acm6SNVObwxoygu6eLOTWIyDAUs5vl/1da8be8cc2d161602a273f5bd73fae00a86a58f997ddeb4b2cd273870cd12814.png)

# This is the video I watched these are the notes:

There can be DPDT switches and TPDT switches:

The P stands for poles and the T stands for throws. The pole indicates a "vertical" line of pins whereas a throw is the connections in a pole between pins, so with 3 pins there can be 2 connections.

This is a diagram for DPDT wiring:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/O3Acm6SNVObwxoygu6eLOTWIyDAUs5vl/5460de0eae32dfc297a558fffe3bad2a4eb5151835456cbcb820d25d5566a705.png)

The two throws that can be used for input and output are either the top 2 or the bottom 2. When the switch is applied, either the system goes through the bottom or top throw.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/O3Acm6SNVObwxoygu6eLOTWIyDAUs5vl/ed12859fe3743ffab990b488bc03757c67f1440336bf7aa1e2bd9370fac63536.png)

The bottom throw has a jumper which directly connects the points in the circuit. This means that when the switch is set to use that part of the circuit, the circuit is closed which allows current to go directly through with "0" resistance.

When the switch is connected to the top throw, the entire system then is able to go through the effect section which allow an effect pedal to be able to go through the system.

I then watched this video for a bit more understanding and to see the wiring but the first diagram was much simpler in describing how the circuitry worked and could apply to me:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/O3Acm6SNVObwxoygu6eLOTWIyDAUs5vl/62553336a75a6f07957831b222eb04a87caa98543e302cb385df6fd9392a9ab1.png)
